assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its compatible norm and Borel measurable structure; rank zero is allowed. Products and the threshold sequence space carry product measurable structures; the record space carries the native disjoint-union structure.
V:E→ℝ is C² on all E. Nonnegative α,β satisfy 0<α≤β, and α‖v‖²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤β‖v‖² for all x,v∈E.

η>0 and βη≤1. These and the preceding potential conditions are the six original analytic callers. The actual flow, bounce, clock, measurable record maps, conserved energy, cap and increment are produced within the proof, never supplied as callers.
y,xRef∈E and initial phase z₀∈E×E are arbitrary. The threshold sequence e:ℕ→[0,∞) is arbitrary, including zeros. It is not assumed to have any probability law; e_n corresponds to source E_(n+1).

An active record is (T,z) with finite T≥0 and phase z. A stopped record has no phase and extended event time ∞. The literal next map tests whether the actual first clock is ∞ before evaluating its finite waiting value, flow or bounce.

The cap C₀ is the displayed actual formula evaluated at the original z₀. The positive-cap and zero-cap branches have their own implication guards. Strict time growth requires a positive threshold and a finite active successor. Arbitrary zero thresholds may repeat an event time with different postjump phases.
units.statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space, including rank zero. Let V:E→ℝ be C², let α,β≥0 satisfy 0<α≤β and α‖v‖²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤β‖v‖² for every x,v, and let η>0 with βη≤1. Fix arbitrary y,xRef∈E, z₀=(x₀,p₀)∈E×E and an arbitrary sequence e_n≥0. Define c=y−η∇V(xRef); Φ_t(x,p)=(c+cos(t)(x−c)+√η sin(t)p, −sin(t)(x−c)/√η+cos(t)p); S(x,p)=(x,p−(2⟨p,∇V(x)−∇V(xRef)⟩/‖∇V(x)−∇V(xRef)‖²)(∇V(x)−∇V(xRef))), using total real division, so a zero normal gives the identity; λ(x,p)=√η max(0,⟨p,∇V(x)−∇V(xRef)⟩); H(x,p)=(η⁻¹‖x−c‖²+‖p‖²)/2; C(z)=√η β√(2H(z))(√(2ηH(z))+‖c−xRef‖); Λ_z(t)=∫₀ᵗλ(Φ_s z)ds for t≥0; and τ_z(e)=inf{t≥0:Λ_z(t)≥e}∈[0,∞], with inf∅=∞. Records are the disjoint union of finite active pairs (T,z) and a phase-free stopped symbol †. Define next_e(†)=†; for an active (T,z), put next_e(T,z)=† if τ_z(e)=∞, otherwise next_e(T,z)=(T+τ_z(e),S(Φ_(τ_z(e))z)). Define r₀=(0,z₀), r_(n+1)=next_(e_n)(r_n), and T_n as the finite time coordinate when r_n is active and ∞ when it is stopped. Then: (1) the initial record is exactly (0,z₀); (2) the successor identity holds, and an active record stops at the next index iff its actual clock is infinite, otherwise it has exactly the displayed active successor; (3) next is jointly Borel in y,xRef,e,r; (4) for each n, r_n is jointly Borel in y,xRef,z₀ and the whole threshold sequence; (5) T_n is jointly Borel in the same inputs; (6) T₀=0 and T_n is nondecreasing; (7) a stopped record at n remains stopped at every n+k; (8) if r_n=(T,z), then H(z)=H(z₀), and for every t≥0 with t<τ_z(e_n), H(Φ_tz)=H(z₀) and 0≤λ(Φ_tz)≤C(z₀); (9) C₀=C(z₀)≥0, C₀>0 implies T_n+max(e_n/C₀,0)≤T_(n+1) for every n, including stopped records, while C₀=0 and an active record with e_n>0 imply that the next record is stopped; (10) for an active r_n=(T,z), e_n=0 gives r_(n+1)=(T,S(z)), while e_n>0 and a finite active successor (T′,z′) imply T<T′. All statements concern the actual finite indexed recursion with fixed y,xRef. No iid realization, almost-sure nonaccumulation, single physical-time phase in the presence of zero thresholds, all-time process, Markov law, invariance, terminal sampler or cost theorem is asserted.

steps.title: Reuse actual flow, bounce and first-clock laws
steps.text: Invoke the compiled laws of the literal harmonic flow, zero-safe bounce/rate and integrated-hazard clock under the same six original analytic callers. Extract joint measurability, flow and bounce energy preservation, nonnegative actual rate, same-energy-layer cap, positive/zero threshold clocks and extended waiting lower bound. No abstract transition or cap certificate is assumed.
steps.lean:
have hf := ActualHarmonicFlow.actual_harmonic_flow_laws hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη
  have hb := ActualBounceRate.actual_bounce_rate_energy_laws hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη
  have hk := ActualHazardClock.actual_integrated_hazard_clock_laws hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη
  have hΦmeas : Measurable (fun a : (E × E) × ℝ × (E × E) =>
      Φ a.1.1 a.1.2 a.2.1 a.2.2) := hf.2.1
  have hΦzero (y xRef : E) (z : E × E) : Φ y xRef 0 z = z := hf.2.2.1 y xRef z
  have hΦH (y xRef : E) (t : ℝ) (z : E × E) :
      H y xRef (Φ y xRef t z) = H y xRef z := hf.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.1 y xRef t z
  have hSmeas : Measurable (fun a : E × (E × E) => S a.1 a.2) := hb.1
  have hSH (y xRef : E) (z : E × E) : H y xRef (S xRef z) = H y xRef z :=
    hb.2.2.2.2.2.2.1 y xRef z
  have hrate0 (xRef : E) (z : E × E) : 0 ≤ rate xRef z :=
    (hb.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.1 xRef z).1
  have hratecap (y xRef : E) (z₀ z : E × E) (hz : H y xRef z = H y xRef z₀) :
      rate xRef z ≤ C y xRef z₀ :=
    ((hb.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.2 y xRef z₀).2 z hz).2.2
  have hτpositive (y xRef : E) (z : E × E) (e : ℝ≥0) :
      0 < e → (0 : WithTop ℝ≥0) < τ y xRef z e :=
    (hk.2.2.2.2.2.1 y xRef z e).2.2.1
  have hτzero (y xRef : E) (z : E × E) : τ y xRef z 0 = 0 :=
    (hk.2.2.2.2.2.1 y xRef z 0).2.2.2
  have hτmeas : Measurable (fun a : (E × E) × (E × E) × ℝ≥0 =>
      τ a.1.1 a.1.2 a.2.1 a.2.2) := hk.2.2.2.2.2.2.1
  have hC0 (y xRef : E) (z : E × E) : 0 ≤ C y xRef z :=
    (hk.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.1 y xRef z).1
  have hwait (y xRef : E) (z : E × E) (e : ℝ≥0) :
      (0 < C y xRef z →
        (Real.toNNReal ((e : ℝ) / C y xRef z) : WithTop ℝ≥0) ≤ τ y xRef z e) ∧
      (C y xRef z = 0 → 0 < e → τ y xRef z e = ⊤) :=
    hk.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.2 y xRef z e
  have hfiniteval (q : ℝ≥0) : (q : WithTop ℝ≥0).untopD 0 = q := rfl
  have hzeroval : (0 : WithTop ℝ≥0).untopD 0 = 0 := rfl

steps.title: Identify the literal finite and stopped recursion branches
steps.text: The initial and successor identities unfold Nat.rec. If the current record is active, split on whether its actual first clock is infinite. The infinite branch is exactly stopped; the other branch contains the finite waiting value and the actual flow followed by bounce.
steps.lean:
have hrec0 (y xRef : E) (z₀ : E × E) (e : ℕ → ℝ≥0) :
      record y xRef z₀ e 0 = Sum.inl (0, z₀) := rfl
  have hrecstep (y xRef : E) (z₀ : E × E) (e : ℕ → ℝ≥0) (n : ℕ) :
      record y xRef z₀ e (n + 1) = next y xRef (e n) (record y xRef z₀ e n) := rfl
  have hbranches (y xRef : E) (z₀ : E × E) (e : ℕ → ℝ≥0) (n : ℕ)
      (a : ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) (ha : record y xRef z₀ e n = Sum.inl a) :
      (record y xRef z₀ e (n + 1) = Sum.inr () ↔ τ y xRef a.2 (e n) = ⊤) ∧
      (τ y xRef a.2 (e n) ≠ ⊤ → record y xRef z₀ e (n + 1) =
        Sum.inl (a.1 + (τ y xRef a.2 (e n)).untopD 0,
          S xRef (Φ y xRef (((τ y xRef a.2 (e n)).untopD 0 : ℝ≥0) : ℝ) a.2))) := by
    rw [hrecstep, ha]
    dsimp only [next]
    split_ifs with ht <;> simp [ht]

steps.title: Prove joint Borel measurability of one actual successor
steps.text: On active inputs, compose the jointly Borel clock with the parameter/phase/threshold projections. The finite-value extraction is Borel; the equality-to-infinity guard is Borel. Compose the actual jointly Borel flow and bounce for the finite branch, then use measurable conditional and disjoint-union maps. A measurable product-over-sum equivalence includes the stopped constant branch.
steps.lean:
have hnextmeas : Measurable
      (fun a : (E × E) × ℝ≥0 × ((ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) ⊕ Unit) =>
        next a.1.1 a.1.2 a.2.1 a.2.2) := by
    let g : ((E × E) × ℝ≥0) × (ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) →
        ((ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) ⊕ Unit) := fun a =>
      if τ a.1.1.1 a.1.1.2 a.2.2 a.1.2 = ⊤ then Sum.inr () else
        Sum.inl (a.2.1 + (τ a.1.1.1 a.1.1.2 a.2.2 a.1.2).untopD 0,
          S a.1.1.2 (Φ a.1.1.1 a.1.1.2
            (((τ a.1.1.1 a.1.1.2 a.2.2 a.1.2).untopD 0 : ℝ≥0) : ℝ) a.2.2))
    have hparams : Measurable
        (fun a : ((E × E) × ℝ≥0) × (ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) =>
          (a.1.1, a.2.2, a.1.2)) :=
      measurable_fst.fst.prodMk (measurable_snd.snd.prodMk measurable_fst.snd)
    have ht0 := hτmeas.comp hparams
    have ht : Measurable (fun a : ((E × E) × ℝ≥0) × (ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) =>
        τ a.1.1.1 a.1.1.2 a.2.2 a.1.2) := ht0
    have hq := ht.untopD (0 : ℝ≥0)
    have hp := hΦmeas.comp (measurable_fst.fst.prodMk
      ((measurable_coe_nnreal_real.comp hq).prodMk measurable_snd.snd))
    have hs := hSmeas.comp (measurable_fst.fst.snd.prodMk hp)
    have hg : Measurable g := measurable_const.ite
      (measurableSet_eq_fun ht measurable_const)
      (measurable_inl.comp ((measurable_snd.fst.add hq).prodMk hs))
    have hsum := hg.sumElim
      (show Measurable (fun _ : ((E × E) × ℝ≥0) × Unit =>
        (Sum.inr () : (ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) ⊕ Unit)) from measurable_const)
    have hm := hsum.comp ((MeasurableEquiv.prodSumDistrib
      ((E × E) × ℝ≥0) (ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) Unit).measurable.comp
      ((measurable_fst.prodMk measurable_snd.fst).prodMk measurable_snd.snd))
    convert hm using 1
    funext a
    rcases a with ⟨⟨y, xRef⟩, e, r⟩
    cases r <;> rfl

steps.title: Prove joint Borel finite record and event-time maps
steps.text: Induct on the finite index. The initial map injects (0,z₀); each successor composes the Borel next map with the previous record and the measurable n-th coordinate of the threshold sequence. The event-time map is the disjoint union of the finite time projection followed by extended-time inclusion and the constant ∞ map.
steps.formula: (y,x_{\rm ref},z_0,e)\longmapsto r_n\text{ and }T_n\text{ are Borel for every }n.
steps.lean:
have hrecordmeas (n : ℕ) : Measurable
      (fun a : (E × E) × (E × E) × (ℕ → ℝ≥0) =>
        record a.1.1 a.1.2 a.2.1 a.2.2 n) := by
    induction n with
    | zero => exact measurable_inl.comp (measurable_const.prodMk measurable_snd.fst)
    | succ n ih =>
      exact hnextmeas.comp (measurable_fst.prodMk
        (((measurable_pi_apply n).comp measurable_snd.snd).prodMk ih))
  have htimemeas (n : ℕ) : Measurable
      (fun a : (E × E) × (E × E) × (ℕ → ℝ≥0) =>
        eventTime a.1.1 a.1.2 a.2.1 a.2.2 n) :=
    ((WithTop.measurable_coe.comp measurable_fst).sumElim measurable_const).comp
      (hrecordmeas n)

steps.title: Carry the original energy through every active finite index
steps.text: Induct on the index, generalizing the candidate active record. At zero the phase is z₀. A stopped predecessor or infinite clock cannot produce an active successor. A finite active successor is SΦ_q(z); flow preservation and bounce preservation give H(SΦ_q(z))=H(z)=H(z₀).
steps.lean:
have henergy (y xRef : E) (z₀ : E × E) (e : ℕ → ℝ≥0) (n : ℕ)
      (a : ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) (ha : record y xRef z₀ e n = Sum.inl a) :
      H y xRef a.2 = H y xRef z₀ := by
    induction n generalizing a with
    | zero =>
      have heq : (0, z₀) = a := Sum.inl.inj ha
      subst a
      rfl
    | succ n ih =>
      rw [hrecstep] at ha
      cases hr : record y xRef z₀ e n with
      | inr u => simp [hr, next] at ha
      | inl b =>
        rw [hr] at ha
        dsimp only [next] at ha
        by_cases ht : τ y xRef b.2 (e n) = ⊤
        · simp only [if_pos ht] at ha
          cases ha
        · rw [if_neg ht] at ha
          have heq := Sum.inl.inj ha
          rw [← heq]
          exact (hSH y xRef _).trans ((hΦH y xRef _ _).trans (ih b hr))

steps.title: Prove nondecreasing event times and stopped absorption
steps.text: At every successor, stopped records remain stopped and have time ∞. An active record either stops, increasing its extended time to ∞, or adds a nonnegative finite wait. Successor monotonicity gives monotonicity on ℕ. A separate induction on k proves that stopping at n persists at n+k.
steps.lean:
have hmono (y xRef : E) (z₀ : E × E) (e : ℕ → ℝ≥0) :
      Monotone (eventTime y xRef z₀ e) := by
    apply monotone_nat_of_le_succ
    intro n
    dsimp only [eventTime]
    rw [hrecstep]
    cases hr : record y xRef z₀ e n with
    | inr u => simp [next]
    | inl a =>
      dsimp only [next]
      split_ifs with ht
      · exact le_top
      · exact WithTop.coe_le_coe.mpr (le_add_of_nonneg_right zero_le)
  have hstopped (y xRef : E) (z₀ : E × E) (e : ℕ → ℝ≥0) (n k : ℕ)
      (hn : record y xRef z₀ e n = Sum.inr ()) :
      record y xRef z₀ e (n + k) = Sum.inr () := by
    induction k with
    | zero => simpa using hn
    | succ k ih => simpa only [Nat.add_succ, hrecstep, ih, next]

steps.title: Use the original energy for every outgoing arc and cap
steps.text: For an active phase z, combine its inherited H(z)=H(z₀) with H(Φ_tz)=H(z). The actual rate is nonnegative, and the already proved same-energy-layer bound gives λ(Φ_tz)≤C(z₀). Since C depends on phase only through H, it also gives C(z)=C(z₀). The displayed arc conclusion keeps its source t<τ guard.
steps.lean:
have harcs (y xRef : E) (z₀ : E × E) (e : ℕ → ℝ≥0) (n : ℕ)
      (a : ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) (ha : record y xRef z₀ e n = Sum.inl a) :
      H y xRef a.2 = H y xRef z₀ ∧
      ∀ t : ℝ≥0, (t : WithTop ℝ≥0) < τ y xRef a.2 (e n) →
        H y xRef (Φ y xRef (t : ℝ) a.2) = H y xRef z₀ ∧
        0 ≤ rate xRef (Φ y xRef (t : ℝ) a.2) ∧
        rate xRef (Φ y xRef (t : ℝ) a.2) ≤ C y xRef z₀ := by
    have hEa := henergy y xRef z₀ e n a ha
    refine ⟨hEa, fun t _ => ?_⟩
    have hEt := (hΦH y xRef t a.2).trans hEa
    exact ⟨hEt, hrate0 xRef _, hratecap y xRef z₀ _ hEt⟩
  have hcap_eq (y xRef : E) (z₀ z : E × E) (hz : H y xRef z = H y xRef z₀) :
      C y xRef z = C y xRef z₀ := by simp only [C, hz]

steps.title: Derive the uniform extended waiting increment
steps.text: For C₀>0, the actual clock bound at the current active phase gives τ_z(e_n)≥e_n/C(z). Replace C(z) by the proved C₀, then add the existing finite event time. An infinite next clock gives the extended inequality automatically. Already stopped records have ∞ on both sides, so the inequality remains valid for every n.
steps.lean:
have hincrement (y xRef : E) (z₀ : E × E) (e : ℕ → ℝ≥0)
      (hC : 0 < C y xRef z₀) (n : ℕ) :
      eventTime y xRef z₀ e n +
        (Real.toNNReal ((e n : ℝ) / C y xRef z₀) : WithTop ℝ≥0) ≤
      eventTime y xRef z₀ e (n + 1) := by
    cases hr : record y xRef z₀ e n with
    | inr u =>
      dsimp only [eventTime]
      rw [hrecstep, hr]
      change (⊤ : WithTop ℝ≥0) + _ ≤ ⊤
      exact le_top
    | inl a =>
      have hCa := hcap_eq y xRef z₀ a.2 (henergy y xRef z₀ e n a hr)
      have hw := (hwait y xRef a.2 (e n)).1 (by simpa only [hCa] using hC)
      rw [hCa] at hw
      dsimp only [eventTime]
      rw [hrecstep, hr]
      dsimp only [next]
      split_ifs with ht
      · exact le_top
      · have hq : (((τ y xRef a.2 (e n)).untopD 0 : ℝ≥0) : WithTop ℝ≥0) =
            τ y xRef a.2 (e n) := by
          induction hτ : τ y xRef a.2 (e n) using WithTop.recTopCoe with
          | top => exact False.elim (ht hτ)
          | coe q => exact congrArg (fun q : ℝ≥0 => (q : WithTop ℝ≥0)) (hfiniteval q)
        change (a.1 : WithTop ℝ≥0) + _ ≤
          ((a.1 + (τ y xRef a.2 (e n)).untopD 0 : ℝ≥0) : WithTop ℝ≥0)
        rw [WithTop.coe_add, hq]
        exact add_le_add le_rfl hw

steps.title: Handle zero original cap with a positive threshold
steps.text: For an active phase, its proved cap equals C₀. If C₀=0 and e_n>0, the actual one-clock zero-cap law says τ_z(e_n)=∞; the exact active stopping equivalence then makes the successor stopped. This conclusion makes no finite-clock assumption.
steps.lean:
have hzerocap (y xRef : E) (z₀ : E × E) (e : ℕ → ℝ≥0)
      (hC : C y xRef z₀ = 0) (n : ℕ) (a : ℝ≥0 × (E × E))
      (ha : record y xRef z₀ e n = Sum.inl a) (he : 0 < e n) :
      record y xRef z₀ e (n + 1) = Sum.inr () := by
    apply (hbranches y xRef z₀ e n a ha).1.mpr
    apply (hwait y xRef a.2 (e n)).2 _ he
    exact (hcap_eq y xRef z₀ a.2 (henergy y xRef z₀ e n a ha)).trans hC

steps.title: Keep zero thresholds and strict positive finite growth distinct
steps.text: For e_n=0, the exact clock is zero and Φ_0 is the identity, yielding (T,Sz) at the same event time. For a positive threshold with an active successor, the clock must be finite; its strict positivity gives a strictly positive finite waiting value, hence T<T′. Collect the ten conclusion groups. Repeated zero-threshold times do not define a single physical-time phase or prove nonaccumulation.
steps.lean:
have hzeroevent (y xRef : E) (z₀ : E × E) (e : ℕ → ℝ≥0) (n : ℕ)
      (a : ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) (ha : record y xRef z₀ e n = Sum.inl a)
      (he : e n = 0) :
      record y xRef z₀ e (n + 1) = Sum.inl (a.1, S xRef a.2) := by
    rw [hrecstep, ha]
    simp only [next, he, hτzero, WithTop.zero_ne_top, ↓reduceIte,
      hzeroval, add_zero, NNReal.coe_zero, hΦzero]
  have hstrictevent (y xRef : E) (z₀ : E × E) (e : ℕ → ℝ≥0) (n : ℕ)
      (a : ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) (ha : record y xRef z₀ e n = Sum.inl a)
      (b : ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) (he : 0 < e n)
      (hb : record y xRef z₀ e (n + 1) = Sum.inl b) : a.1 < b.1 := by
    have ht : τ y xRef a.2 (e n) ≠ ⊤ := by
      intro ht
      have hs := (hbranches y xRef z₀ e n a ha).1.mpr ht
      rw [hb] at hs
      cases hs
    have hq : 0 < (τ y xRef a.2 (e n)).untopD 0 := by
      have hp := hτpositive y xRef a.2 (e n) he
      induction hτ : τ y xRef a.2 (e n) using WithTop.recTopCoe with
      | top => exact False.elim (ht hτ)
      | coe q => simpa only [hτ, hfiniteval, ← WithTop.coe_zero,
          WithTop.coe_lt_coe] using hp
    have hupdate := (hbranches y xRef z₀ e n a ha).2 ht
    rw [hb] at hupdate
    have heq := Sum.inl.inj hupdate
    have hbtime := congrArg Prod.fst heq
    rw [hbtime]
    exact lt_add_of_pos_right _ hq
  exact ⟨hrec0, fun y xRef z₀ e n =>
    ⟨hrecstep y xRef z₀ e n, hbranches y xRef z₀ e n⟩,
    hnextmeas, hrecordmeas, htimemeas,
    fun y xRef z₀ e => ⟨rfl, hmono y xRef z₀ e⟩, hstopped, harcs,
    fun y xRef z₀ e => ⟨hC0 y xRef z₀, hincrement y xRef z₀ e,
      hzerocap y xRef z₀ e⟩,
    fun y xRef z₀ e n a ha => ⟨hzeroevent y xRef z₀ e n a ha,
      hstrictevent y xRef z₀ e n a ha⟩⟩
steps.detail: Exact contiguous compiled public BODY. The eleven literal definitions and preceding facts remain in scope. All stochastic nonaccumulation and global-process consumers remain separate.

units.lean_statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space, including rank zero. Let V:E→ℝ be C², let α,β≥0 satisfy 0<α≤β and α‖v‖²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤β‖v‖² for every x,v, and let η>0 with βη≤1. Fix arbitrary y,xRef∈E, z₀=(x₀,p₀)∈E×E and an arbitrary sequence e_n≥0. Define c=y−η∇V(xRef); Φ_t(x,p)=(c+cos(t)(x−c)+√η sin(t)p, −sin(t)(x−c)/√η+cos(t)p); S(x,p)=(x,p−(2⟨p,∇V(x)−∇V(xRef)⟩/‖∇V(x)−∇V(xRef)‖²)(∇V(x)−∇V(xRef))), using total real division, so a zero normal gives the identity; λ(x,p)=√η max(0,⟨p,∇V(x)−∇V(xRef)⟩); H(x,p)=(η⁻¹‖x−c‖²+‖p‖²)/2; C(z)=√η β√(2H(z))(√(2ηH(z))+‖c−xRef‖); Λ_z(t)=∫₀ᵗλ(Φ_s z)ds for t≥0; and τ_z(e)=inf{t≥0:Λ_z(t)≥e}∈[0,∞], with inf∅=∞. Records are the disjoint union of finite active pairs (T,z) and a phase-free stopped symbol †. Define next_e(†)=†; for an active (T,z), put next_e(T,z)=† if τ_z(e)=∞, otherwise next_e(T,z)=(T+τ_z(e),S(Φ_(τ_z(e))z)). Define r₀=(0,z₀), r_(n+1)=next_(e_n)(r_n), and T_n as the finite time coordinate when r_n is active and ∞ when it is stopped. Then: (1) the initial record is exactly (0,z₀); (2) the successor identity holds, and an active record stops at the next index iff its actual clock is infinite, otherwise it has exactly the displayed active successor; (3) next is jointly Borel in y,xRef,e,r; (4) for each n, r_n is jointly Borel in y,xRef,z₀ and the whole threshold sequence; (5) T_n is jointly Borel in the same inputs; (6) T₀=0 and T_n is nondecreasing; (7) a stopped record at n remains stopped at every n+k; (8) if r_n=(T,z), then H(z)=H(z₀), and for every t≥0 with t<τ_z(e_n), H(Φ_tz)=H(z₀) and 0≤λ(Φ_tz)≤C(z₀); (9) C₀=C(z₀)≥0, C₀>0 implies T_n+max(e_n/C₀,0)≤T_(n+1) for every n, including stopped records, while C₀=0 and an active record with e_n>0 imply that the next record is stopped; (10) for an active r_n=(T,z), e_n=0 gives r_(n+1)=(T,S(z)), while e_n>0 and a finite active successor (T′,z′) imply T<T′. All statements concern the actual finite indexed recursion with fixed y,xRef. No iid realization, almost-sure nonaccumulation, single physical-time phase in the presence of zero thresholds, all-time process, Markov law, invariance, terminal sampler or cost theorem is asserted.
units.lean_proof: Reuse actual flow, bounce and first-clock laws; Identify the literal finite and stopped recursion branches; Prove joint Borel measurability of one actual successor; Prove joint Borel finite record and event-time maps; Carry the original energy through every active finite index; Prove nondecreasing event times and stopped absorption; Use the original energy for every outgoing arc and cap; Derive the uniform extended waiting increment; Handle zero original cap with a positive threshold; Keep zero thresholds and strict positive finite growth distinct
